articles.title: Why did the Supreme Court block the ‘easier’ route to constitutional amendment?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of Nepal issued an order suspending two provisions of the House of Representatives' rules that would have created a faster pathway for amending the constitution. The court halted the ‘easier’ route after raising five key constitutional questions concerning procedural legitimacy, separation of powers, the scope of parliamentary authority, the protection of fundamental rights, and the potential for political instability. Legal experts and lawmakers are debating the implications of the ruling, which underscores the judiciary’s role in safeguarding constitutional integrity while highlighting tensions between the legislative agenda and judicial oversight.

articles.title: Australia cracks down on student and backpacker visas to curb migration
articles.summary: The Australian government announced stricter rules for international student and backpacker visas as part of a broader effort to lower net migration. The policy aims to reduce annual net migration from roughly 300,000 to 225,000 by 2028, tightening eligibility and stay conditions for these visa categories.

articles.title: Foreign secretary says Nepal will press climate justice case at UN
articles.summary: Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced that Nepal will advance a climate‑justice case at the United Nations, seeking loss‑and‑damage funding and enhanced adaptation support for the Himalayas. He called for greater international attention to the region’s vulnerability and urged the UN and donor nations to address the climate impacts threatening Nepal’s ecosystems and communities.

articles.title: Nepal Electricity Authority offers relief to families of flood-missing workers
articles.summary: The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) announced financial assistance for families of employees who went missing during recent floods. A one-time payment of Rs 50,000 will be given to families of missing workers, while relatives of permanent staff will receive half of the employee's starting salary for up to six months. The relief aims to support affected households while the NEA assesses the broader impact of the disaster on its workforce.

articles.title: India warns new US tariffs over Russian oil could hit ties, vows to protect energy security
articles.summary: India warned that new U.S. tariffs on Russian oil could strain bilateral ties and pledged to safeguard its energy security. The warning may complicate ongoing trade negotiations with Washington, as Indian refiners seek relief to manage existing Russian oil purchases.

articles.title: Agriculture exports from Karnali top Rs3.64 billion, but livestock imports drain Rs951 million
articles.summary: Karnali Province recorded agricultural exports worth Rs3.64 billion, shipping 77,495 tonnes of crops and other farm produce. Despite this export growth, the province continued to import livestock products, spending Rs951 million, indicating that local livestock production remains insufficient to meet demand. The disparity highlights both the province's strength in crop trade and ongoing challenges in the livestock sector.

articles.title: Federal affairs ministry tops list of ministries with most corruption complaints
articles.summary: The Federal Affairs Ministry has emerged as the top recipient of corruption complaints in Nepal, with over 3,000 cases filed with the anti‑graft agency during the last fiscal year. The surge highlights growing concerns over governance and accountability within the ministry and its regional offices, prompting calls for stricter oversight and reforms.

articles.title: Bridges gone, roads damaged, villages cut off from relief
articles.summary: Severe damage to bridges and roads in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts has isolated villages, hindering relief efforts. Helicopters and temporary crossings are currently being used to deliver food and essential supplies to the cut‑off communities. Officials emphasize that restoring the damaged infrastructure must be an immediate priority to ensure long‑term access and recovery.

articles.title: Nepal lost a para taekwondo star. Australia just won gold
articles.summary: Former Nepali para‑taekwondo world champion Shrijana Ghising has obtained Australian citizenship ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics and has already secured a gold medal for Australia. Her switch highlights a growing trend of Nepali athletes seeking better support abroad, prompting coaches in Nepal to warn that she may not be the last to leave. While Australia celebrates her success, Nepal mourns the loss of a top talent and faces concerns over retaining elite sportspeople.

articles.title: Tatopani reopening unlikely before festive season. Traders urge Beijing talks
articles.summary: The Tatopani border crossing with China is unlikely to reopen before Nepal's Dashain festival, causing traders to press the government for talks with Beijing. With two northern crossings disrupted, cargo is being rerouted through the Korala pass, where high transport costs and inadequate infrastructure are further delaying shipments. The situation threatens supply chains ahead of the major festive season.

articles.title: Nepal’s next big MMA star Yuki is fighting in China’s JCK on Saturday
articles.summary: Nepalese mixed martial artist Angdembe, known as ‘The Gurkha’ and popularly called Yuki, will compete in a high‑stakes bantamweight bout against Chinese fighter Buhuogubu at the JCK‑123 event in Lüliang, Shanxi, China on Saturday.

articles.title: Government’s ‘ego’ holding football hostage, ANFA says as crisis deepens
articles.summary: The All Nepal Football Association (ANFA) has accused Nepal's sports ministry and the National Sports Council (NSC) of letting personal ego impede the sport, warning that the crisis is worsening as the Men’s SAFF Championship deadline of September 30 approaches. ANFA says the football federation is burdened with over Rs100 million in debt, and government inaction threatens the country's participation in the regional tournament. The dispute highlights tensions between football administrators and government bodies over funding and management.

articles.title: Answer the mountain’s call
articles.summary: Nepal government needs to respond to disasters with greater accountability and leadership.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s youth-led government inherited the toughest job in Asia
articles.summary: Nepal’s newly formed youth‑led government has inherited what analysts call the toughest portfolio in Asia. Sandwiched between nuclear powers India and China, the administration must navigate delicate diplomatic balances while confronting severe domestic challenges. Rapid glacier melt and other climate impacts threaten water supplies, agriculture, and tourism, demanding urgent adaptation policies. Economic recovery, infrastructure rebuilding after recent earthquakes, and rising unemployment add to the pressure on the inexperienced leaders. The article argues that the government's survival will hinge on its ability to manage external geopolitical tensions and internal climate‑driven crises simultaneously.

articles.title: Why the RSP must heed the Supreme Court’s interim order
articles.summary: The ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) is urged to comply with the Supreme Court's interim order, avoid political overreach, learn from past mistakes, and respect judicial authority.

articles.title: JE is killing more adults in Nepal as vaccination only covers children
articles.summary: Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is increasingly causing deaths among adults in Nepal, as the current immunisation program only targets children. Health experts warn that people over 30 are now at higher risk and face a high fatality rate if unvaccinated. They are urging the government to expand the JE vaccination programme to include adults, especially those above 30, to curb the rising mortality.

articles.title: Bhotekoshi floods disrupt schooling for 14,500 children in three districts
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi River to flood, inundating villages in three Nepalese districts and forcing schools to serve as emergency shelters. As a result, schooling for about 14,500 children has been disrupted, with more than 9,400 students directly affected by the disaster. The use of school buildings for temporary housing has delayed the resumption of classes for thousands of learners, highlighting the broader impact of the floods on education and community recovery efforts.

articles.title: Exhibit review: When thoughts, memories and emotions step out of the mind
articles.summary: The exhibition showcases works by fifteen artists who translate their inner thoughts, memories, and emotions into tangible pieces. The diverse installations explore personal struggles, recollections, and broader themes such as politics, power dynamics, and aspirations for a better future. By turning intangible mental experiences into visual forms, the show invites viewers to reflect on their own inner worlds and the societal forces that shape them.

articles.title: More complaints, fewer wins for CIAA in corruption cases
articles.summary: The anti-graft agency CIAA received over 40,500 complaints in the last fiscal year, but its conviction rate at the Special Court dropped to 51.92%, indicating fewer successful prosecutions despite more complaints.

articles.title: Wagle seeks India’s support for post-flood reconstruction
articles.summary: During his inaugural overseas trip as Nepal's finance minister, Wagle met with Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to request assistance for rebuilding infrastructure devastated by the Bhotekoshi floods. The discussions also covered enhancing trade, attracting investment, and improving connectivity between the two nations. Wagle emphasized the urgency of post‑flood reconstruction and sought India's technical and financial support to accelerate recovery efforts.

articles.title: How Deuba lost his own inner circle to Thapa
articles.summary: Senior leader Purna Bahadur Khadka opted for dialogue instead of a party split, prompting dozens of Prime Minister Deuba’s loyalists to shift to Sanepa for the upcoming general convention. The move has effectively stripped Deuba of his inner circle, with many aligning behind Thapa, signaling a significant realignment within the party ahead of the convention.

articles.title: China presses Iran to help rein in Houthis after Saudi appeal
articles.summary: China is urging Iran to assist in restraining Houthi attacks in the Red Sea after Saudi Arabia appealed for help, as the assaults threaten key shipping lanes and oil routes vital to China's economic interests.

articles.title: Wagle set for high-level talks in New Delhi
articles.summary: Nepal's Finance Minister Wagle is on a three‑day visit to India. On the second day in New Delhi, he will hold high‑level talks with the Indian Foreign Minister to discuss bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest, including economic cooperation, trade, and regional security.

articles.title: Two teenage girls rescued while being taken to India on false job promise
articles.summary: Two 16‑year‑old girls from Bardiya district were intercepted in Banke district after authorities received a tip about a suspected human‑trafficking scheme that intended to move them to India under a false job promise. Police halted the girls at the Suiya border point, rescuing them before they could be taken across the border. The incident highlights ongoing cross‑border trafficking concerns and the effectiveness of local tip‑offs and law‑enforcement coordination.

articles.title: Jute harvest keeps Sunsari farmers busy
articles.summary: In Sunsari district, Nepal, the jute harvest is in full swing as farmers dedicate weeks to cutting, retting, stripping and drying the fibre before it reaches market. The article outlines the labor‑intensive steps involved and underscores jute’s role as a key cash crop for local agricultural livelihoods.
